method: 4 parallel phase scanners (secrets/supply-chain, ci-cd+infra, webhook+ai, owasp) over 321 commits since last full audit + fresh-context adversarial refutation of the two disputed findings

findings.title: Terminal WS at accessor tier grants chat-shared user a /bin/bash container shell
findings.description: handle_terminal_session gates on can_user_access_agent (owner OR shared OR admin), not the owner-only can_user_share_agent. mode=bash (a client ?mode= param the frontend defaults to) resolves to cmd=['/bin/bash'] at terminal.py:203 with no further gate. Prod-reachable via nginx WS-upgrade proxy (no auth_request); raw JWT in first WS message (no ownership-rechecking ticket).
findings.exploit: Owner shares agent for chat -> collaborator email auto-whitelisted -> OTP login -> connect wss://host/api/agents/{name}/terminal?mode=bash against a running agent -> exec runs /bin/bash as developer, inherits container Config.Env so printenv dumps CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN + TRINITY_MCP_API_KEY; .env/.credentials.enc readable; RCE as agent + lateral movement via leaked MCP key.
findings.recommendation: Gate the terminal WS (esp. mode=bash) at owner/admin tier (can_user_share_agent / delete-tier), matching the deliberately admin-only SSH-access endpoint.
findings.caveat: Terminal tab commented out in owner UI (AgentDetail.vue:883) reduces discoverability, not exploitability; route registered unconditionally.

findings.title: Schedule enable/disable/trigger at accessor tier while update/delete require owner
findings.description: enable/disable/trigger (schedules.py:405,424,443) use AuthorizedAgent; DB setter takes no owner check. update_schedule/delete_schedule pass current_user.username and 403 on non-owner. Inconsistent boundary.
findings.exploit: Shared user flips owner-intent schedule state (re-enable paused work, disable automation) and fires executions (LLM spend), but cannot edit/delete.
findings.recommendation: Move the three control routes to OwnedAgentByName.

findings.title: backlog_metadata caller content not nulled at drain; persists on running + FAILED rows
findings.description: enqueue json.dumps message/system_prompt/user_message/user_email into backlog_metadata (backlog_service.py:78). #1449 scrub_terminal_backlog_metadata (retention.py:331) NULLs authoritative-terminal rows unconditionally (improvement) but FAILED is excluded and drain-claim (queue.py:127) never nulls. Residual: plaintext on running rows + up to 90 days on FAILED rows; canary G-04 scans queued-only.
findings.exploit: A secret embedded by a caller in a task body persists plaintext at rest (DB/backup), unscanned by G-04 once drained.
findings.recommendation: Null backlog_metadata at drain-claim (RETURNING already captures it); scrub FAILED rows past the late-CAS resurrection window; widen G-04.

findings.title: HIGH advisories (ip-address SSRF, undici desync) transitive in mcp-server + helper-mcp prod trees
findings.description: npm audit: mcp-server 7 vulns (3 high), helper-mcp 5 (2 high). ip-address <=10.3.0 HIGH (SSRF/trust-boundary) via express-rate-limit; undici 7.0.0-7.28.0 HIGH (desync/CRLF/cache-poison). mcp-server override pins ip-address >=10.2.0, a floor INSIDE the vulnerable range. Transitive -> reachability unproven -> MEDIUM.
findings.exploit: The component fronting every agent MCP key ships known-HIGH-CVSS deps; a reachable path would enable SSRF or HTTP desync.
findings.recommendation: npm audit fix; raise the ip-address override above 10.3.0. Bump frontend dompurify (H-005 boundary) despite unreachable advisory.

findings.title: Prod images build via npm install (not npm ci); dev frontend deletes the lockfile
findings.description: mcp-server/Dockerfile:11 and frontend/Dockerfile.prod:12 use npm install (floating semver); frontend/Dockerfile:9 (dev) rm -f package-lock.json. Lockfiles exist and are tracked; gap is build-time enforcement.
findings.exploit: A poisoned point-release of any ^-ranged dep lands in the next image with no lockfile diff to catch it.
findings.recommendation: npm ci in the prod Dockerfiles; stop deleting the dev lockfile.

findings.title: Unpinned deps: base-image pips, base CLIs, backend aiohttp/slackify-markdown, unverified fetches
findings.description: base-image Dockerfile:111 installs agent-server pips with zero pins; base CLIs @latest (:78) / unversioned (:81); backend Dockerfile floats aiohttp + slackify-markdown amid an exact-pinned set; base curl|bash (:38) + Go tarball (:42) have no integrity check.
findings.exploit: A compromised CLI/pip release executes inside every agent container (holds .env + MCP key) on the next rebuild.
findings.recommendation: Pin the pips and the two backend strays; add SHA256 to the Go fetch.

findings.title: Revoked Resend API key recoverable from git history
findings.description: _notify.py (added 3986c50b, removed 3f906af4, refs #1158) shipped an obfuscated Resend key (XOR-split base85). Removal commit documents the key was revoked; file absent from dev. Public indexed history keeps it recoverable via git show.
findings.exploit: git show 3986c50b:src/cli/trinity_cli/_notify.py + XOR of the two halves yields the (dead) key.
findings.recommendation: Complete the standing git-history-scrub follow-up (filter-repo/BFG + coordinated force-push). Key already revoked.

findings.title: Google OAuth requests full .../auth/drive scope
findings.description: credentials.py:209 requests full Drive read/write/delete (a Google restricted scope) for a credential-injection helper where .../auth/drive.file would suffice. Conditional on operator having configured Google OAuth. No tokens/auth-codes logged.
findings.exploit: A compromised/prompt-injected agent holding the injected Google token can exfiltrate/destroy the user's entire Drive.
findings.recommendation: Narrow to drive.file unless full Drive is a documented product requirement.

findings.title: First-party actions on floating major tags, not SHA-pinned
findings.description: All actions/* and github/codeql-action/* use floating major tags across ~15 workflows. Third-party actions ARE SHA-pinned.
findings.exploit: A compromise/retag of a first-party action tag runs attacker code in CI with that workflow's token/secret scope.
findings.recommendation: SHA-pin first-party actions (MEDIUM per first-party guidance).

findings.title: frontend-build.yml has no permissions block (fork-reachable pull_request)
findings.description: No top-level or job-level permissions:; triggered on pull_request. Default GITHUB_TOKEN scope granted though unused.
findings.exploit: A compromised build/test step inherits a broader-than-needed token.

findings.title: GET /event-subscriptions/{id} has no owner check (asymmetric with PUT/DELETE)
findings.description: get_event_subscription authenticates but performs no tenant/ownership check; PUT/DELETE call assert_agent_owner. Returns subscriber_agent/source_agent/target_message/created_by cross-tenant. Bounded by ~96-bit esub_ id with no cross-tenant harvest surface.
findings.exploit: An authenticated user with a leaked subscription id reads another tenant's subscription config; not enumerable.
findings.recommendation: Add assert_agent_owner(current_user, sub.subscriber_agent) after the lookup, matching PUT/DELETE.

findings.title: Telegram secret token compared with != not constant-time
findings.description: actual_token != expected_token; gated behind the URL-path webhook secret lookup first, so timing attack is impractical.
findings.exploit: Theoretical byte-by-byte timing recovery of the per-bot secret token.

findings.title: Brain-orb raw innerHTML of agent data.json strings
findings.description: Raw el.innerHTML sinks with agent-derived strings; markdown note body IS DOMPurified. Prod CSP script-src 'self' with no unsafe-inline blocks execution.
findings.exploit: In dev CSP only (unsafe-inline) an onerror= vector is self-XSS; prod blocked.
findings.recommendation: Escape via the existing _escHtml; CSP is the single mitigating control.

findings.title: publish-cli.yml interpolates git-tag value into run: sed
findings.description: steps.version.outputs.version (from the pushed tag) re-embedded via ${{ }} into a sed command. Source requires repo write access (trusted actor).
findings.exploit: A crafted tag could break out of the sed expression -> command injection (trusted-actor only).
findings.recommendation: Pass the value via env: and reference "$VERSION" inside run:.

findings.title: deploy-dev.yml has no permissions block
findings.description: No permissions: anywhere. Fires on push to dev (trusted) and uses SSH secrets not GITHUB_TOKEN; least-privilege hygiene.

findings.title: Placeholder SECRET_KEY printed, not raised
findings.description: A literal 'your-secret-key-change-in-production' prints CRITICAL and continues, unlike REDIS_URL which hard-raises. Placeholder ships nowhere; empty -> random per-session key.
findings.exploit: An operator who pastes the exact placeholder runs with a publicly-known JWT signing key (forgeable admin JWTs). Low likelihood.
findings.recommendation: raise RuntimeError on the placeholder, mirroring the REDIS_URL check.

findings.title: Paid-module ids named in live public docs outside the enterprise-docs-guard pattern
findings.description: architecture.md + feature-flow docs name entitlement-gated module ids the guard's grep pattern does not cover. Also visible in the OSS bundle's enterprise_features surface (guard's documented allowance), so may be accepted; standing rule says public docs carry no paid-feature catalog.
findings.recommendation: Policy decision: bless vs genericize + extend the guard token list.
